proposed.paraphrase: SANHA classifies lecithin (E322) as Halaal, with soybean as the predominant commercial source (also egg and leguminous seeds); the overwhelming majority of commercial E322 is plant-derived, so undisclosed-source lecithin is very widely accepted as halal though alternative origins exist.

proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation (AHF) — 'Are Emulsifiers Halal?' (Azmi Anees)
proposed.paraphrase: AHF states soy and sunflower lecithin (E322) are plant-derived and generally considered halal, but lecithin extracted with ethanol-based solvents or of unclear origin may require verification / halal certification — i.e. unspecified-source lecithin is widely accepted yet warrants confirmation.

researcherNote: E322 unspecified origin = grade 2 (Questionable — widely accepted). ~70-80% of commercial lecithin is soy/plant and all authorities treat lecithin as presumptively halal, so unspecified sits at 'widely accepted' (grade 2) — not grade 3/4 — with a minor verify-source/ethanol-extraction caveat (rare egg/animal variants exist). Two independent tier-1 sources (SANHA + AHF). APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
